10:45.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
10:45.targetText: for even the Son of Man did not come to be ministered to, but to minister, and to give His life [as] a ransom for many.”

groups.note: The accusative ransom is the predicative/appositional description of the given life; LSV marks that actual noun relation with bracketed as. No independent Greek as word is invented.

10:46.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἰερειχώ. Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ Ἰερειχὼ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλου ἱκανοῦ ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου Βαρτιμαῖος, τυφλὸς προσαίτης, ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν.
10:46.targetText: And they come to Jericho, and as He is going forth from Jericho with His disciples and a great multitude, a son of Timaeus—Bartimaeus the blind—was sitting beside the way begging,

groups.note: The genitive absolute going-forth participle is rendered as a temporal as ... is going forth clause; English as expresses that actual construction.
N1904 coordinates the genitive-absolute participants Jesus and His disciples; LSV expresses that accompaniment as with His disciples, not a general equivalence of καί and with.
N1904 names him a beggar with προσαίτης; LSV renders that occupation as the participle begging, while the sitting predicate retains its own verb.

10:47.sourceText: καὶ ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζαρηνός ἐστιν ἤρξατο κράζειν καὶ λέγειν Υἱὲ Δαυεὶδ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλέησόν με.
10:47.targetText: and having heard that it is Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out, and to say, “The Son of David—Jesus! Deal kindly with me”;

10:48.sourceText: καὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ πολλοὶ ἵνα σιωπήσῃ· ὁ δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν Υἱὲ Δαυείδ, ἐλέησόν με.
10:48.targetText: and many were rebuking him that he might keep silent, but the more abundantly he cried out, “Son of David, deal kindly with me.”

10:49.sourceText: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Φωνήσατε αὐτόν. καὶ φωνοῦσιν τὸν τυφλὸν λέγοντες αὐτῷ Θάρσει, ἔγειρε, φωνεῖ σε.
10:49.targetText: And Jesus having stood, He commanded him to be called, and they call the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage, rise, He calls you”;

The Greek active plural imperative call is reported by LSV’s passive to be called. The actual calling head is retained without claiming an additional Greek passive verb.
